prerequisites: Mathematics: Curve discussion (power, exponential, logarithmic functions)
Chemistry: Periodic table, chemical compounds, thermodynamic terms (enthalpy, free energy, phase rule), corrosion reactions (electrochemical potentials, passivation)
Mechanics: Stress, moment of inertia, elastic bending beams, deflection of a plate

Physics: Physical properties (electrical and thermal conductivity, specific heat, magnetic properties, Peltier effect), induction, crystal structures (hcp, bcc, fcc), microscopy, characteristic X-ray radiation
For the 2,0/2,0 LU Werkstoffprüfung 1, positive completion of the StEOP (initial study and orientation phase) is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the causes of different material properties and quantify them using material characteristic values.
Master the basics of material selection and recognize how material properties can be influenced in the manufacturing process.
Acquire basic knowledge of application possibilities of metals, polymers, and ceramics.
Explain the causes of different material properties comprehensibly.
Reliably calculate material characteristic values.
Present the basics of material selection in a structured way.
Systematically analyze the influenceability of material properties in the manufacturing process.
Describe the application possibilities of metals, polymers, and ceramics in a practical way.
Clearly distinguish material categories and structural changes (alloys, plastics, ceramics, glasses, composite materials).
Correctly calculate characteristic values for elasticity, strength, ductility, and toughness for various types of stress.
Investigate material damage due to environmental conditions (wear, corrosion) based on typical features.
Explain chemical and thermodynamic principles for plastic and alloy types understandably.
Perform simple material testing methods (tensile test, toughness, hardness, materialography) professionally.
Appropriately select non-destructive testing methods for given tasks.
Apply analytical thinking by systematically investigating material behavior and cause-effect relationships (e.g., structure → property → application).
Derive suitable materials for technical requirements.
Demonstrate abstraction ability by transferring models (e.g., crystal structures, phase diagrams) to real technical problems.
Safely handle data and diagrams (e.g., stress-strain curves, phase diagrams).
Correctly interpret measurement results and experimental data.
Evaluate materials from sustainability, cost, and safety perspectives.
Develop problem-solving competence.
Think interdisciplinarily and establish connections to mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemistry, and physics.
Think practically by linking theory and industrial application.

syllabus_topics: Material categories and differences, structural changes (alloys, plastics, ceramics, glasses, composite materials)
Elasticity, strength, ductility, and toughness under various types of stress
Material damage due to environmental influences (wear, corrosion)
Chemical and thermodynamic principles for plastic and alloy types
Simple material testing methods (tensile test, toughness, hardness, materialography)
teaching_methods: Students develop the execution of testing procedures together with supervisors
Practical exercises for applying theoretical content

assessment_methods.method: Protocols for exercises and lab parts (supplementary)

assessment_rules: Performance control is carried out through written and oral examinations with calculation examples and theoretical questions. For a positive module evaluation, both partial exams must be successfully completed. In the case of clear written results, the oral examination part can be waived. Tests and protocols for the exercise and laboratory parts can supplement the performance evaluation.
